lead.title: A plan, not a chat log
lead.description: Plans, milestones, tasks, and acceptance criteria live in one local SQLite journal that your screen and your agent's CLI both read.

lead.title: Milestones are lanes
lead.description: A lane names its wave and role. Dispatch prints the worktree command for the lane and the command that starts the next ready task.

lead.title: Proof on every criterion
lead.description: Evidence, commits, and pull requests attach to the criterion they prove. Missing proof is marked stale, never hidden.

support.title: A guided first run
support.description: Placement, agents, hooks, model tiers, and role effort live in one wizard that shows every file before it writes.

support.title: Tiers, models, and effort
support.description: Fast, standard, and deep tiers map to each host's models. Roles can also set low, medium, or high effort.

support.title: Lanes in waves
support.description: Waves run in order and lanes in parallel up to the plan's cap. A lane holds one doing task at a time.

support.title: One worktree per lane
support.description: lpui plan worktree prints and registers the checkout commands. lazyplan never creates, merges, or removes one itself.

support.title: Claims that prevent collisions
support.description: Leases, touch-points, and expiry keep parallel agents off each other's files.

support.title: Sessions and handoffs
support.description: Hooks record each agent session. Comments and notes carry the handoff, so the next worker resumes instead of asking for a briefing.

support.title: Review before it ships
support.description: A plan arrives as a draft with anchored comments, questions, and change requests. The agent revises against them, and promotion waits until every note is answered.

support.title: A control room for what needs you
support.description: Health, drift, open questions, and blocked work surface in one line, so you know where to look.

support.title: Trust hubs, not a wall of text
support.description: Criteria, evidence, questions, references, and approvals are selectable hubs on every row.

support.title: Evidence with the command
support.description: Record the command, exit code, commit, and proving task. The latest record decides whether a criterion is proven.

support.title: Source trail
support.description: Walk from task to repo, commit, changed file, and pull request. Missing proof is marked stale.

support.title: Version in the taskbar
support.description: The running version sits at the right edge. A newer release adds an arrow; click it or press U to download and verify.

support.title: Local-first and private
support.description: SQLite on your machine, no account, no cloud. Export or import any time.

support.title: Keyboard-first
support.description: A fast tree, command palette, and history. The mouse is optional.

support.title: A log, not a toast stack
support.description: Ordinary notices collect in a session log with their time and source; only startup and update notices interrupt. Warnings and errors badge the taskbar until you read them.

support.title: Themes and icon palettes
support.description: Mocha, void, and latte themes, plus classic, orbit, blocks, marks, and ASCII glyph sets. Both choices survive restarts and keep every row aligned.
